narratives.Description: Correct repo identity after the public deftai clone
narratives.Overview:
`deftai/directive-training` is now a **public** DeftAI repository (duplicate of `3Ci-Consulting/directive-training` `master`). Several identity and policy claims still describe the 3Ci private original.

That leftover is now false and agents will follow it.

## Current facts
- Remote: `https://github.com/deftai/directive-training`
- Visibility: public
- Owner: `deftai`
- Not the Directive framework source (`deftai/directive`)

## Stale claims to recut
- `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` `plan.narratives.ProjectRules`: "This repository belongs to 3Ci and must remain private" plus "do not change its visibility or remote settings" and "do not ... create issues or pull requests in deftai/directive"
- Same file `Maintenance` / overview narratives that name 3Ci as sole owner
- `AGENTS.md` unmanaged header: "Private, self-directed Directive training for 3Ci engineers"
- `README.md`: "Private, self-directed Directive training for 3Ci engineers"

## Out of scope unless a later issue expands it
Do not rewrite the whole curriculum in this issue. Lab fiction (`3Ci Lab Learner`), historical 3Ci Actions links in `references/`, and `COST-ESTIMATE.md` 3Ci-tooling cost notes can stay until someone decides whether the public course is DeftAI-branded, 3Ci-internal, or both.

## Acceptance
- Project identity in xBRIEF, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md` matches the public `deftai` remote
- No remaining rule that this working tree must stay private or 3Ci-owned
- Safety rules that still matter (no learner work in this tree, no real client/secrets data) stay

Refutation target: project identity in xBRIEF, AGENTS.md, and README.md must match the public deftai remote and must drop 3Ci-private ownership and visibility rules.

Re-verified at dispatch SHA `cbdb7f337511b78d49530e6800e30bb3150165c9` via `git show`, not a moving branch. `origin` is `git@github.com:deftai/directive-training.git`. REST `repos/deftai/directive-training`: `owner=deftai`, `visibility=public`, `private=false`, `fork=false`.

The first conjunct survives. The second does not, if it means deleting visibility controls. False current-state claims that this GitHub repo is 3Ci-owned and must remain private are agent-followed leftovers. The remote-as-identity lock in the same ProjectRules paragraph is not a leftover; it is the control that keeps identity matched to origin after the recut.

### 1. Drop-visibility-rules deletes the identity lock (`blocks-the-design`)

Evidence: `plan.narratives.ProjectRules` at that SHA is one paragraph. The false current-state is the opening sentence: this repository belongs to 3Ci and must remain private. The next sentences are the existing mechanism: treat the configured Git remote as repository identity; do not change its visibility or remote settings; this is not `deftai/directive`; leave USER.md in place; keep Greptile disabled; keep learner work and secrets out of this tree. The issue stale-claims bullet quotes "do not change its visibility or remote settings" as a recut target. AGENTS.md session orientation already names `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` as project identity, and session routing loads it.

Failure mode: a recut that treats the whole blob as stale removes the mutation lock. An agent with git or gh then retargets origin or flips visibility, including back to private. Identity correction becomes identity mutation. Closing that on reviewer attention is not a control.

Disposition: this target cannot bind as "drop visibility rules." Split ProjectRules. Correct the current-state sentence to the measured public `deftai` remote. Keep the remote-as-identity lock and the still-true safety sentences. Do not add a new identity file.

### 2. Forge identity is not content owner or audience (`sharpens-framing`)

Evidence: the same xBRIEF still names 3Ci as curriculum owner (`Overview`, `Maintenance`), learner audience (`Audience`), and `plan.title`. Issue out-of-scope parks whether the public course is DeftAI-branded, 3Ci-internal, or both, while stale-claims lists Overview/Maintenance 3Ci-owner sentences. Acceptance only forbids a remaining rule that this working tree must stay private or 3Ci-owned. README's still-valid safety line forbids learner work in a 3Ci business or client repository; that is not tree ownership.

Failure mode: the recut rewrites audience and content owner as DeftAI and silently decides the parked branding question, or it leaves Overview saying the curriculum is private and 3Ci-owned so forge identity still mismatches.

Disposition: recut forge identity and the false privacy current-state. Park content-owner and learner-audience until a branding issue. Overview can state a public `deftai` repo without claiming 3Ci no longer authors the course.

### 3. Three-file inventory misses a live privacy rule (`sharpens-framing`)

Evidence: `maintainers/CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md` still has "Visibility: private/internal" and "Keep the course private." README Maintainers points there as the maintenance contract. Completed xBRIEF `2026-09-14-remove-claim-labels-and-3ci-module-language` OutOfScope explicitly parked project identity and private-repository governance. `labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md` "fixture must remain private" is disposable-lab policy, which the issue already parks.

Failure mode: the three named files recut; acceptance "no remaining rule that this working tree must stay private" stays false because the maintainer contract still binds anyone README sends there.

Disposition: include those two maintainer sentences in this recut, or narrow acceptance to the three files and name the leftover.

### 4. npm private is not GitHub visibility (`sharpens-framing`)

Evidence: root `package.json` is `"private": true` with no `repository` field. `scripts/verify-modules-2-3.mjs` (assert at the training-package check), `scripts/verify-modules-4-5.mjs`, and `scripts/verify-module-6.mjs` all require that flag with message "the training package must remain private." Lab fixtures have the same npm lock.

Failure mode: a grep for "must remain private" flips npm `private` to match public GitHub. Those content contracts fail, and the training package becomes npm-publishable. That is not GitHub visibility.

Disposition: leave `package.json` `"private": true`. Do not treat those verifier messages as this issue's leftover.

### 5. Injection / swarm lens (`footnote`)

The target changes identity and agent-followed policy, so the lens applies. The in-ceiling thread had no extra embedded instructions. The deterministic control is the existing ProjectRules remote lock, not a new gate. AGENTS.md unmanaged header already says edit the one-liner (#2065); do not add Status/Next.

### 6. Copy, not a GitHub fork (`footnote`)

REST `fork=false`, `parent=null`. "Duplicate of 3Ci-Consulting/directive-training" is a copy. Do not assume fork-sync.

Road-not-taken: a new identity artifact — rejected; session routing already loads AGENTS.md plus PROJECT-DEFINITION. Full DeftAI rebrand — rejected; the issue parks it. Flip `package.json` private — rejected; npm lock.

Steelman of the target: leftover 3Ci-private current-state in the three files will be followed as policy now that origin is public `deftai`; recut those current-state claims. That half holds. What would flip it: REST showing private 3Ci ownership. Measured facts do not.
